_note: The FAMILY's moments (session P1, GDD 4.9.5; format in README.md). Senders: parent / parent:mum / parent:dad / parent:athlete (the one who ran) / sibling / family. The family's attitude (data/cast.json attitudes, condition `family`) decides which moments fit and which text variant is used. Session L3a (the sort, docs/L3_SORT.md, user 2026-10-25): most are FEED messages that ask nothing (no replies; only story state in `effects`, e.g. the family coming round); five are INVITATIONS into a free-time slot; six are STORY BEATS on the Sunday planner whose replies take free-time slots (`slots`). The 'against' family comes round from good signs the game counts (cast.json warmth: a PB, a good report card), not from replies. Every storylet lists what it touches (`touches`, data/moments.json touches) and has the conditions that guard it. Ages 14-16 (P2 adds 16-17). Every person is fictional.

text: Dinner was at six. Your plate is in the microwave, second shelf.
We ate without you again. There's pasta in the fridge.

text.text: You came home at eight and ate standing up. Athletes need proper meals, you know that better than anyone.

text: We're going to see Grandma on {weekday}. She asks about your running every time. Coming?
Grandpa turns 75 on {weekday}. The whole family will be there. You're coming, right?

replies.label: Of course I'm coming
replies.result: They wanted to hear everything about your races.

replies.label: I'd rather stay home
replies.result: She won't be around forever, you know.

text: We saw the result! Well done. Pizza on Friday, you pick the toppings.

text.text: {pb}! I ran faster at your age, but not by much. Proud of you.
A good race. Champions don't celebrate small steps for long, but today you can.
My colleagues saw it on the club's website. I told them: that's my kid. Well done!
The neighbour saw your result in the paper. So, well done, I suppose.

text: I saw the result. There's ice cream in the freezer, if you want it.

text.text: I looked at the results online. The next one will go better. They usually do.
One bad race. Your grandfather used to say: lose, learn, come back.
Maybe this is a sign to concentrate on school for a while.

text: In my day we ran 10 × 400 every Tuesday, no matter what. I hope your coach gives you enough speed work.
When I was your age my coach made us run the stadium stairs until we couldn't feel our legs. Different times.
Arms relaxed, hands low. That's the one thing I wish someone had told me at fourteen.
I looked at the results. Next time, think about where you want to be at the bell.
Good, but I think you left something in the tank.
Champions train when nobody is watching. I hope you did your stretching today.
I made the national team because I never missed a session. Remember that.
Your room is a mess. Discipline starts at home.
Running, running. Your cousin is learning to code, you know.
So many practices a week. I worry about your future.
Nobody makes a living from running around a track in Finland.
You have a test on {tomorrow}. Stay in and study on {weekday} evening. For me.
Tests first, running later. {weekday} evening is for the books, please.

replies.label: I'll study that evening
replies.result: Good. I made you tea.

replies.label: I'll keep my evening as it is
replies.result: We'll see who's right when the grades come.

text: I read about you in the local paper today. Your name was there. I didn't know you were that good. I'd like to come and watch you one day.
I took the day off for {meet}. Don't say anything to your aunt, she thinks I'm at the dentist.
Your coach's message said 'threshold run'. I looked it up. It sounds dangerous.
You run in circles for an hour and call it 'easy'. I will never understand.
Your aunt asked what a personal best is. I said it's like a high score.

text.text: Skiing on {weekday}? The tracks at the lake are finally open.
A hike on {weekday}? The national park, sandwiches, the whole family.
Ice skating on the lake on {weekday}? The ice is thick enough now.

replies.label: Count me in
replies.result: Cocoa and the whole family. A good day.

replies.label: Not this time
replies.result: Next time then.

text: You're staying in bed today. I've told the school. There's soup on the stove.
Fever. Bed. No arguments. I'll bring you tea.
You've been quiet all week. I know you hate not running.
I know you hate this. Film night whenever you want one. No sports films.
I race on {weekday}. Come and watch? You can carry my bag, little one.
{weekday}, 1500 m. If you come, I'll run faster. Probably.

replies.label: I'll be there
replies.result: Thanks for the snacks. And the shouting.

replies.label: I'll stay home
replies.result: Fine. I'll text you how I won.

text: {pb}, huh. At your age I ran faster. Not for long though, I can see that.
OK, that was fast. Don't let it go to your head. {parent} already told everyone.
Before {meet}: don't look at the others in the call room. Look at your shoes. Works for me.
Tip for {meet}: the first 100 always feels easy. It's a trap.
Happy birthday! There's cake later. And a present that might be shoe-shaped.
Happy birthday, {name}! Who would have believed you'd be this tall. Cake later.
Merry Christmas! The rice porridge is on. Ham and casseroles later.
Christmas Eve. The Christmas peace is declared on TV at noon, the same as every year.
New Year's Eve! Tin melting at the kitchen table, fireworks at midnight for whoever is awake.
Last day of the year. We'll melt tin and see your future. A medal shape, I'm sure.
Juhannus at the cottage! We leave on Thursday, back on Sunday. Bonfire, sauna, the lake. Take your running shoes: the gravel road round the lake is 7 km.
Midsummer at the cottage again, Thursday to Sunday. The whole family. It wouldn't be juhannus without you.

replies.label: The whole weekend
replies.result: Great! We leave on Thursday.

replies.label: I'll come on Saturday
replies.result: Take the bus, then. We'll pick you up.

replies.label: I'll stay home
replies.result: Alone at juhannus? Well, it's your choice.

text: The cottage is free this week. No internet, the lake, Grandpa's boat. The forest roads are endless if you take your running shoes.
Cottage week again: your cousins are coming. The whole week, or just the weekend.

replies.label: The whole week!
replies.result: Wonderful. The water is warm already.

replies.label: Just the weekend
replies.result: Better than nothing.

replies.label: I'll stay home
replies.result: We'll miss you. Grandpa will ask.

text: Cottage week! The water is 21 degrees. The sauna is warm by six.
Morning at the cottage. Fog on the lake. Grandpa is already fishing.
Rippikoulu registration closes this month. Most of your class goes to a summer camp. Which one do you want? June, July, or the day school in town?
The church sent the confirmation school letter. A camp week in June or July, or the day school here in town. Your friends are choosing now.

replies.label: The June camp
replies.hint: the camp week in June takes that week's evenings and weekend
replies.result: June it is.

replies.label: The July camp
replies.hint: the camp week in July takes that week's evenings and weekend
replies.result: July, then. After juhannus.

replies.label: The day school in town
replies.hint: you sleep at home: no evenings taken
replies.result: Fine. The day school is in June, here in town.

replies.label: I don't want to go
replies.result: It's your decision. Your grandmother will ask, though.

text: Camp starts on Monday. Your bag is in the hall. Running shoes too, I suppose.
A week without you from Monday. The house will be quiet.
Grandma is making her cake for your rippijuhlat. Twenty relatives, coffee and cake. Wear the nice shirt.
The rippijuhlat invitations are out. Your uncle will ask about your running all afternoon.
The joint application opens soon. Have a think about where you want to go. {counsellor}, the study counsellor, can help.

text.text: An urheilulukio would make sense. Morning practice, coaching. I wish I'd had that.
A good general upper secondary school first, sport second. That's what we think.
Your report card! Up from last time. We're proud of you, school and sport both.
Better grades than last time. Good. Discipline in one place shows in the other.
The grades went up. Fine. If running helps you study, keep running.

text: Report card day. About the same as before: an average of {avg}.

text.text: Same as last time. Steady. That's fine, as long as it stays there.
Your grades dropped. We hope it isn't the training.
Lower grades. A top athlete is good at managing time.
This is what we were afraid of. Grades down, running up.

text: Your first report card of the year: an average of {avg}.

text.text: First report card: {avg}. Not bad for someone who trains this much.
{avg}. We expected more, honestly. We'll see how the spring goes.

text: You got your first choice! Congratulations! We'll have cake. Then the practical side.

text.text: Your first choice! I'm so proud. This is where it starts for real.

text: Not your first choice, but you have a place. It's a good school.
The results are out. Not the first wish, but a place. Sometimes the second road is the right one.
No place this time. I'm so sorry. We'll look at the other options together.

text.text: No place. I said the grades matter. But we'll find a way. We always do.

text: Saturday sauna is warm. Löyly, a cold shower, the evening news.
Sauna first, then sausages. A proper Saturday.
Grandma called. She read your result in the local paper and cut it out.
Grandma asked about your next race. She wants to come and watch one, with a thermos.

invite.title: The 800 m final on TV on {weekday}?

text: The championships are on TV. The 800 m final is on {weekday} evening. Watch it together?
I don't understand half of it, but I'll watch the 800 m final with you on {weekday}. Deal?

replies.label: Yes! I'll explain everything
replies.result: You explained the bell lap three times. It was worth it.

replies.label: I'll watch it on my own
replies.result: Suit yourself.

text: Lapland this winter break? Monday to Thursday: skiing, a cabin, the northern lights maybe.
A ski trip this winter break: Levi, Monday to Thursday, cross-country trails right outside the door.

replies.label: Yes, Lapland!
replies.result: Booked. Bring wool socks.

replies.label: I'd rather stay home
replies.result: Next year, then.

beat.title: The autumn break in the country

text: The autumn break is this week. A few days at Grandma's in the country? The forest roads are lovely in October.
Autumn break plans: a few days at the cottage, mushrooms and quiet. Coming?

replies.label: Sounds nice
replies.result: Good. Pack something warm.

replies.label: I'll stay in town
replies.result: OK. Your friends will be happy.

beat.title: A week in Tallinn and Pärnu

text: We're off to Tallinn and Pärnu this week: the hotel, the beach, the old town. The beach is good for easy runs.
The summer trip is this week: the ferry on Monday, then Pärnu beach. Your cousins say hi.

replies.label: Yes, I'm coming
replies.result: Pack your running shoes.

replies.label: I'll stay with Grandma
replies.result: If that's what you want.
